decisive_items: repeated right-sided epistaxis without obvious trauma
Multiple small capillary malformations on trunk (hyperpigmented)
response.rationale: Recurrent unexplained epistaxis with dropping hemoglobin, a nasal vascular malformation with capillary dilation, and cutaneous capillary lesions strongly fit HHT; the main competing neurocutaneous syndromes do not explain the prominent nasal bleeding/anemia or lack the required CNS/limb findings.

rejected.why: Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber syndrome requires limb overgrowth and typically port-wine/venous malformations; no limb hypertrophy is present and nasal epistaxis/anemia is unexplained.
Ehlers-Danlos syndrome lacks the nasal vascular malformation, capillary malformations, and developmental/dysmorphic phenotype; typical skin/joint hypermobility is absent.
Sturge-Weber syndrome is less likely because cranial CT showed no leptomeningeal/calcification abnormality and it does not account for recurrent epistaxis or the nasal mucosal vascular malformation.
PHACE syndrome requires posterior fossa/arterial anomalies or a segmental hemangioma; cranial CT was normal and recurrent epistaxis/nasal vascular lesion remains unexplained.
